title: improv·artist · chromatic (Gerhard Richter)
mutation_directive: improv artist: chromatic via Gerhard Richter

improv_extras.practice: color-grid charts, squeegee abstracts; randomness as method

v1.feedback: Strong concept-to-form link: Chladni eigenmodes as Richter squeegee layers is genuinely inventive, and the per-layer mode offsets creating chromatic fringing at nodal boundaries is the kind of detail that rewards close looking. The flat-plane presentation is conceptually correct but visually modest — consider a more oblique camera angle (lower Y, closer Z) to let the impasto height differences read as physical paint texture rather than mere color variation. Mode transitions should include a directional 'squeegee sweep' disruption wave crossing the plate rather than uniform interpolation, which would make the Richter reference visceral rather than merely structural.

v2.feedback: The Chladni-to-squeegee concept is genuinely smart — chromatic fringing at nodal boundaries is a faithful translation of Richter's pigment separation. Two things to push: the impasto z-displacement is nearly invisible at ±0.003 units from the oblique camera; tripling that amplitude (and modulating it by eigenmode amplitude) would let the key light actually sculpt ridges the way Richter's squeegee leaves paint peaks. Second, additive blending on earth tones over a near-black ground makes the plate read dimmer than it should — consider switching to NormalBlending with a slightly lighter plate base (0x1a1714) so the four strata read as opaque pigment layers rather than luminous gas.
